"Create a polished, lightweight 2D top-down sci-fi extraction and exploration game called LOST SIGNAL: DEEP RECOVERY.

GAME CONCEPT:
The player explores an abandoned futuristic research facility to recover valuable technology, rare artifacts, energy cells and classified data.

CORE GAMEPLAY:
- Explore interconnected rooms and corridors.
- Search abandoned laboratories, lockers and storage containers.
- Collect loot with different rarity levels.
- Avoid security drones and environmental hazards.
- Manage limited battery power and inventory space.
- Find the extraction elevator and escape safely.
- Keep recovered items only after successful extraction.

PROGRESSION:
Create a small personal base where players can:
- Upgrade their scanner to detect nearby loot.
- Increase battery capacity.
- Expand backpack inventory.
- Improve movement speed.
- Unlock new research facility sections.

WORLD DESIGN:
Include:
- Research laboratories.
- Storage rooms.
- Server rooms.
- Maintenance tunnels.
- Restricted research areas.

Randomize loot locations and some room connections between missions to improve replayability.

ENEMIES AND HAZARDS:
Add security drones that patrol the facility and detect nearby players. The player should be able to hide, evade and escape.
Include electrical failures, darkness, damaged floors and other environmental hazards.

VISUAL STYLE:
- 2D top-down perspective.
- Dark sci-fi atmosphere.
- Charcoal, dark blue and teal colors.
- Orange warning lights.
- Glowing computer screens.
- Detailed but lightweight pixel-art graphics.
- Smooth player animations.

USER INTERFACE:
Include health, battery, inventory, item rarity, minimap, mission objective, extraction indicator and base upgrade menus.

CONTROLS:
- WASD or arrow keys for movement.
- E for interaction.
- Mobile virtual joystick and touch-friendly buttons.
- Responsive layout for desktop and mobile.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:
- Use HTML5 Canvas and JavaScript.
- Deliver a complete playable game in a single self-contained HTML file.
- No external APIs, servers, paid libraries or external assets.
- Optimize for low-end hardware and mobile browsers.
- Implement collision detection, functional interactions and persistent local saves.
- Make every button functional.
- Include a restart option.

IMPORTANT:
Do not create a static demonstration or menu-only prototype.
Prioritize a complete gameplay loop: exploration, loot collection, resource management, extraction and permanent progression.
Build a small but polished game rather than a large unfinished one.

---

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
